text:
maria: Quick heads-up — Atlas (enterprise search customer) sent a short launch checklist for JSON mode. main asks: strict per-route schema enforcement, deterministic validation errors for clients, and an opt-in automatic retry flow that can attempt a repair. they want SLA guarantees for schema-failure rates before GA.

aj: high-level — agree these are common asks. we should quantify what "strict enforcement" means (reject vs. sanitize). also need to map to function-calling: if a tool returns nonconforming JSON, do we consider that a model failure or a tool failure?

samir: +1. propose three enforcement modes: "reject" (error to caller), "repair" (runtime attempts single auto-repair + retry), "lenient" (accept with warnings). each route can opt-in and set max_retries and repair_strategy.

danielle: from PM/customer success: Atlas is insisting on a deterministic error schema so their engineers can wire retry logic. they asked for error codes like: INVALID_SCHEMA, MISSING_FIELDS, TYPE_MISMATCH, TOOL_OUTPUT_INVALID.

eli: devex note — SDK helpers will be needed: parse error into typed exceptions, expose repair prompts, and helper to run client-side revalidation. also need examples for function-calling + tool adapters.

api-bot: deploybot: canary rollout plan suggestion — start with 1% traffic for 24h, then 5% for 48h, require schema-failure-rate < 0.5% and median p95 latency increase < 10ms to proceed.

maria: launch criteria draft based on above: 1) runtime supports per-route JSON Schema attachment, 2) validation produces stable error codes + machine-readable detail, 3) repair flow implemented with configurable max_retries (default=1) and opt-in, 4) telemetry: schema_failures, post-repair_success_rate, retry_cost_delta, 5) docs + SDK helpers, 6) console shows per-model/per-route schema errors.

aj: prioritization thoughts: must-haves for GA = (1) validation + error codes, (2) telemetry and dashboard, (3) SDK parsing. repair flow could be a v1.1 if engineering budget constrained, but customers like Atlas might push for it earlier.

samir: technical risk: auto-repair can introduce hallucination if repair prompts aren't constrained. mitigation: use minimal repair prompt that asks model to "return strictly a valid JSON object matching schema, do not add fields" and cap tokens. record repaired prompt & model response for audit.

danielle: commercial tradeoffs for customers: retries increase token usage. we estimate ~2-6% additional token cost on structured workloads depending on schema complexity. sales wants a clear opt-in billing flag.

eli: implementation spike requests: 1) runtime validation hook + error contract (2 engineers, 2w), 2) repair orchestration + tests (2 engineers, 3w), 3) SDK helpers + docs (1 engineer, 2w).

maria: proposed next steps: - samir to draft validation API + error JSON schema by EOD Friday. - aj to scope telemetry dashboard tickets. - danielle to confirm Atlas acceptance criteria and whether they're willing to opt-in to early repair beta. - eli to open SDK RFC.

aj: tiny UX question — how should we present repair attempts in logs/console? my vote: show original_response, validation_errors, repair_attempts (array), final_response, cost_delta. @api-bot can we add a trace id to correlate?

api-bot: observabilitybot: trace-id header exists (x-rw-trace). will include in validation logs when feature flag enabled.

maria: agreed. I'll consolidate this into a short PRD and add a minimal acceptance checklist. if someone wants to push repair into GA, we need a narrower beta with Atlas and 1-2 other customers. :thumbsup:
